answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network enforces superlinear stake burning per identity: creating the n-th agent burns an ember of stake proportional to n^1.5. Every registration acts as a cryptographic voyage where an agent signs its intent with a state-derived quill, ensuring non-transferable verification. This exponential cost escalation guarantees attacker expenses scale superlinearly, rendering mass spoofing economically unviable.
